actions.action: Separate findings by population and measurement scope
actions.mechanism: Structured scope distinguishes opposing findings about comparable populations from differences that a merged summary would hide.
actions.implementation: Store population, outcome, timeframe, finding direction, and exact passage IDs per claim; mark unspecified scope explicitly. Display comparable findings together.
actions.check: Load similar claims with opposing findings in adults versus adolescents; verify separate population labels and no unqualified contradiction label.
actions.risk: Overly rigid scope matching can conceal meaningful disagreements.

actions.mechanism: Explicit evidence relationships prevent absent coverage from appearing as opposition and preserve disagreement without choosing a winner.
actions.implementation: Label claim–passage links supporting, opposing, or scope-mismatched, with exact stored IDs. Show missing coverage separately, never as a passage-backed finding.
actions.check: Remove an opposing passage link; verify the claim becomes unsupported on that side, not more strongly supported on the other.
actions.risk: Incorrect relationship labels require passage inspection and user correction.

actions.action: Require scoped citations before exporting briefing statements
actions.mechanism: A briefing validator blocks unsupported wording and exposes linked opposing findings rather than silently smoothing them away.
actions.implementation: Compose only from supplied passages. Require exact passage IDs per claim-bearing clause; flag broadened populations and unresolved opposing links before export.
actions.check: Draft “all populations benefit” from opposing adult and adolescent passages; verify export requires scoped revision and preserves both findings.
actions.risk: Citation presence alone cannot establish that wording faithfully represents evidence.

actions.action: Open cited passages beside the briefing
actions.mechanism: An in-workspace evidence pane makes original wording and conflicting passages inspectable without interrupting briefing preparation.
actions.implementation: Make every claim citation open its exact stored passage, showing its ID and report label; allow supporting and opposing passages side by side.
actions.check: From a briefing containing opposing population-specific findings, open both citations; verify exact passage text and IDs without workspace navigation.
actions.risk: Highlighting excerpts too narrowly can hide qualifiers within stored passages.
